1.explanation:
1. src/languages.js
   • This module exports the list of language plugins that Prettier will bundle. To include the Cherow parser plugin in Prettier’s internalPlugins, you must require or import a new Cherow-based plugin here.

2. src/language-js/index.js
   • The JavaScript language definition registers which parsers are available for JavaScript files (babel, flow, espree, typescript, etc.). You need to add “cherow” to the parsers list and define a getter for parsers.cherow so that Prettier can call Cherow’s parseScript under the parser name “cherow.”

3. src/main/parser.js
   • This core resolver reads opts.parser (string or function) and maps that to the appropriate plugin’s parse function. To support opts.parser = “cherow” you must ensure resolveParser can locate and return the Cherow parser, falling back to the existing Babel/Flow resolver when a file has a Flow pragma or “.js.flow” extension.

4. src/standalone.js
   • In the standalone bundle, Prettier assembles all bundled plugins via languages.map into its internalPlugins. You must include the Cherow plugin so that standalone.format(text, { parser: 'cherow' }) works in the browser worker and Node.js standalone mode.
1.bug_scenario: The attached screenshot is a speed benchmark comparing various JavaScript parsers on large JS libraries (jQuery, Angular, React, TypeScript, etc.). It shows that Cherow is about 40% faster than Babylon (the parser Prettier currently uses via @babel/parser). The user wants Prettier to switch to Cherow for parsing JavaScript by default to speed up format-on-save scenarios, while still falling back to the Babel-based Flow parser for files that use Flow syntax (".js.flow" or contain a @flow pragma).
